objective: Treat historical races as if they are future races by physically/logically separating information available before the race from outcomes and payouts, then replaying chronologically.

allowed: historical racecard snapshot proven to represent pre-race values
objective line partition and solo-rider count when objectively sourced
pre-race recent-form statistics whose cutoff is proven before the race
timestamped PRE odds for purchase-gate research only
prohibited: current rider profile backfilled into historical race without point-in-time proof

OUTCOME_ESCROW.rule: Prediction and buy/no-buy decisions must be hash-frozen before this lane is joined.

chronological_replay.principle: At replay date T, only PRE and outcomes from dates strictly earlier than T may influence any adaptive model state.
chronological_replay.recommended_blocks: walk-forward chronological blocks; preserve a final untouched block for scientific evaluation
chronological_replay.same_day_cross_leakage: No use of later-race results to predict an earlier-start-time race; if same-day adaptive updates are studied, order strictly by official start time and preregister it.

hypotheses_to_add.question: Are final races less predictable or economically different after controlling for field-strength parity?
Does solo-rider presence increase placement dispersion or create 2nd/3rd value?
hypotheses_to_add.requires: objective PRE line partition and solo_count

hypotheses_to_add.question: Does individual-strength predictability remain high out of time and which market, if any, retains value?
Does score-gap/dispersion identify when head prediction is easier while companion positions scatter?
Which of 3renhuku 1pt, conditional max2, and 3rentan third-spread wins on recovery, drawdown, and stability?

promotion_rule: No candidate becomes a practical profit rule from burned or newly searched historical data alone. Candidate must be frozen and reproduce on later untouched/prospective data.
